query: Section 232 steel aluminum tariff exclusions status

statements.text: On April 30, 2025, BIS publicized a rule implementing the resulting Section 232 Inclusions Process. Submissions are accepted in two-week windows three times per year.
Yes, GSP and AGOA can be claimed on any goods that are subject to a valid Section 232 exclusion. However, GSP or AGOA cannot be claimed on entries subject to Section 232.

Pursuant to Presidential Proclamations 10895 and 10896 of February 10, 2025, Commerce is no longer processing Section 232 Exclusion Requests effective 11:59 PM ET on February 10, 2025, and is no longer accepting or issuing exclusions from the Section 232 Steel and Aluminum Tariffs.

All General Approved Exclusions (GAEs) and country-level ‘alternative arrangements’ to the Section 232 Steel and Aluminum Duties (including exemptions, absolute quotas, and tariff-rate quotas) were revoked effective 12:01 AM Eastern Time on March 12, 2025.
Updated 6/26/2025. Section 232 steel and aluminum duties are only due on entries for consumption.

(ix) The additional duties imposed by headings 9903.01.25, 9903.01.35, 9903.01.39, and 9903.01.43-9903.01.77 shall not apply to derivative aluminum products provided for in headings 9903.85.04, 9903.85.07, 9903.85.08 and 9903.85.09.

(vii) The additional duties imposed by headings 9903.01.25, 9903.01.35, 9903.01.39, and 9903.01.43-9903.01.77 shall not apply to derivative iron or steel products provided for in headings 9903.81.89, 9903.81.90, 9903.81.91, 9903.81.92 and 9903.81.93.

Updated 6/11/2025. If the steel and/or aluminum derivative is classified in one of the new HTS classifications subject to Section 232 steel and/or aluminum derivatives duties on or after March 12, 2025, and the good is made exclusively from steel melted and poured in the United States, or exclusively made from aluminum smelted and cast in the United States, then the good is not subject to Section 232 steel and/or aluminum duties.

Section 232 Steel and Aluminum Inclusions Proclamations 10895 and 10896 of February 2025, among other actions, applied the Section 232 Steel and Aluminum Tariffs to additional steel and aluminum downstream (or “derivative”) products, calculated either on the full value of the product or the value of the steel and aluminum content of the product depending on the HTSUS Classification.

IEEPA Reciprocal Tariffs and Section 232
Articles and derivatives of steel and aluminum subject to Section 232 duties are excluded from the reciprocal tariffs; pursuant to heading 9903.01.33, HTSUS.
An exclusion is generally valid for one year from the date of signature, or until the granted quantity has been exhausted (whichever comes first).
